ideas.hypothesis: After a widely used governance index or rating is published in a country, firm practices converge toward the index items, including items with no measurable performance effect, which points to performative rather than efficiency-driven convergence.

sources.role: mechanism: claims about corporate governance as performative statements that stabilize particular corporate architectures
setting: governance quality and the convergence question in SEE countries
finding: debate over global convergence of governance disclosure practices

ideas.test: Hand-code annual-report governance practices for listed firms in 2-3 countries before and after a national governance index was introduced; difference-in-differences comparing adoption of index items with comparable practices that the index leaves out, then relate adoption to later performance.
ideas.disconfirming: Index and non-index practices converge at the same rate, or convergence happens only for items that raise performance.

ideas.hypothesis: Independent directors of firms in regions with stronger Confucian traditions cast fewer dissenting votes and resign in protest less often, because deference to authority weakens monitoring.

sources.role: mechanism: boards' reflexive obedience to legitimate authority such as the CEO
setting: Chinese listed firms and relationship contracting (guanxi)
mechanism: bias and conflict pressures on monitors and gatekeepers

ideas.test: Chinese listed firms 2004-2018 using mandatory disclosure of independent director dissent; measure Confucian intensity by the density of historical Confucian academies or temples near headquarters; logit of dissent on Confucian density with firm, industry and year controls.
ideas.disconfirming: No association, or more dissent in more Confucian regions.

ideas.hypothesis: Unwinding cross-shareholdings raises the sensitivity of CEO turnover to poor performance, because stable cross-held blocks shield managers from discipline.

sources.role: setting/mechanism: Japanese cross-shareholdings with banks and old-boys'-club boards
mechanism: link between effective monitoring and performance

ideas.test: Japanese listed firms 1995-2015 with cross-shareholding ratios and CEO turnover; panel logit of turnover on ROA interacted with the cross-shareholding ratio, using bank-driven unwinding after limits on bank shareholdings as an instrument.
ideas.disconfirming: Turnover-performance sensitivity does not change with cross-shareholding levels or after unwinding.

ideas.hypothesis: Stricter disclosure requirements reduce value-destroying related-party transactions only in firms that already have strong governance; in weakly governed firms disclosure alone leaves RPT volume and market reactions unchanged.

sources.role: finding: strict disclosure complements but does not substitute for strong governance in protecting minority shareholders
measure: governance disclosure index for listed firms

ideas.test: Exploit a disclosure rule change on RPTs (e.g., India's 2013 Companies Act or Chinese exchange rules) with firm-level RPT data; triple difference by pre-reform governance score, with RPT volume and announcement returns as outcomes.
ideas.disconfirming: RPTs fall equally in weakly and strongly governed firms, or disclosure alone reduces them in weak firms.

ideas.hypothesis: The performance effect of board independence is concentrated in firms with low information costs (high analyst coverage, simple structures), because outside directors cannot monitor well when information is costly.

sources.role: mechanism: information costs of monitoring arrangements shape strategy and performance
setting: board attributes and effectiveness
measure: ROE and stock performance as outcomes

ideas.test: US listed firms around the 2002-2003 exchange independence rules; difference-in-differences comparing firms forced to add independent directors, split by pre-rule analyst coverage and business segment count.
ideas.disconfirming: Independence effects are equal or larger in high-information-cost firms.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms with employee representatives on the supervisory board show lower pay dispersion between executives and median workers without lower profitability.

sources.role: mechanism: governance mechanisms and the distribution of income to workers
setting: German two-tier model and co-governance
setting: comparison of governance models

ideas.test: German firms around the 500- and 2000-employee codetermination thresholds; regression discontinuity using executive pay disclosures and linked employer-employee wage data.
ideas.disconfirming: No discontinuity in pay ratios at the thresholds, or lower profitability offsets any compression.

ideas.hypothesis: Higher D&O insurance coverage lowers the quality of voluntary governance disclosure, because insured directors face less personal liability for opacity.

sources.role: measure: governance disclosure scores
mechanism: disclosure as protection for minority shareholders

ideas.test: Firms in markets where D&O coverage is disclosed (e.g., Canada, Taiwan, China); regress disclosure index scores on coverage limits, using insurance-market hardening as an instrument.
ideas.disconfirming: No relation, or more coverage goes with better disclosure.

ideas.hypothesis: Interlocking directors spread biased strategic choices: firms that share a director with a firm that recently overpaid in an acquisition are more likely to make similar value-destroying acquisitions.

sources.role: mechanism: bias and conflicts of interest among monitors
mechanism: board deference and loyalty

ideas.test: BoardEx interlock networks and SDC M&A data; compare acquirer announcement returns of firms tied to recent overpaying acquirers with matched untied firms, using director deaths or retirements as exogenous breaks in ties.
ideas.disconfirming: Interlocked firms are no more likely to make value-destroying deals.

ideas.hypothesis: Under high environmental uncertainty larger boards improve performance by adding advice and resources, while under low uncertainty larger boards hurt performance through coordination costs.

sources.role: mechanism: external business environments affect performance through governance
measure: board attributes and shareholder value

ideas.test: Compustat/BoardEx firms 2000-2018; uncertainty measured by industry sales volatility; regress Tobin's q on board size x uncertainty with firm fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: The effect of board size does not vary with uncertainty.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms whose main bank holds equity or a board seat suffer less tunneling by controlling shareholders, seen in fewer related guarantees and lower abnormal intercorporate loans.

sources.role: mechanism: bank as the basis of external governance through contingent governance
setting: ownership structure of Chinese listed firms

ideas.test: Chinese listed firms 2003-2018 using CSMAR data on bank shareholdings and bank-affiliated directors and on other receivables and guarantees to related parties; panel regressions with firm fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Bank governance is unrelated to tunneling measures.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries whose corporate law moved toward shareholder primacy saw faster increases in top wealth shares, through higher payouts and equity-based pay.

sources.role: setting: return of shareholder primacy over stakeholder claims
mechanism: governance rooted in politics shapes income and wealth distribution
mechanism: governance claims with political-economy consequences

ideas.test: Panel of about 25 OECD countries 1980-2015 combining leximetric shareholder protection indices with World Inequality Database top wealth shares; panel difference-in-differences around legal changes.
ideas.disconfirming: Shifts toward primacy are unrelated to wealth concentration.

ideas.hypothesis: Employee representatives on compensation committees reduce the pay-for-luck part of executive compensation.

sources.role: mechanism: governance processes for an equitable share for workers
setting: executive compensation as a target of governance reform
mechanism: double agency relationship that includes employees

ideas.test: German and Scandinavian listed firms with committee composition data; estimate pay sensitivity to industry-wide (luck) shocks by whether worker representatives sit on the committee.
ideas.disconfirming: Pay-for-luck is the same with or without worker representatives.

ideas.hypothesis: China's WTO accession improved disclosure transparency more in listed firms in export-exposed and import-competing industries than in sheltered industries.

sources.role: setting: WTO accession as a spur to better governance in Chinese firms
measure: application of the transparency principle by listed companies
setting: governance of Chinese listed companies

ideas.test: Chinese listed firms 1998-2006 using exchange disclosure ratings or analyst forecast dispersion; difference-in-differences by industry tariff-cut exposure.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference in transparency improvement by exposure.

ideas.hypothesis: In SOEs undergoing mixed-ownership reform, managerial equity incentives raise productivity only when non-state shareholders also gain board seats.

sources.role: setting: proposed governance model for SOE reform
finding: inconclusive links between ownership, boards and performance in China
mechanism: improving internal governance first

ideas.test: Chinese listed SOEs 2006-2019 with equity incentive plan announcements and board composition; difference-in-differences on TFP, interacted with non-state board seats.
ideas.disconfirming: Equity incentives raise TFP regardless of board seats, or not at all.

ideas.hypothesis: When a sustainability-oriented institutional blockholder enters, target firms' governance and ESG scores improve within two years more than after entry by a conventional blockholder.

sources.role: mechanism: investors defined broadly; governance models used to judge sustainability commitment
setting: roles of stakeholders in governance

ideas.test: 13F ownership data with responsible-investment signatory status and ESG ratings 2006-2018; event study comparing new 5% blockholder entries by signatories with entries by non-signatories.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference in post-entry improvement.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms with more anti-takeover provisions invest more in long-horizon sustainability projects without lower returns, consistent with protection from short-term market pressure.

sources.role: mechanism: corporate governance and sustainability commitment
setting: tension between shareholder primacy and stakeholder claims
mechanism: monitoring regimes shape corporate strategy

ideas.test: US firms with entrenchment/governance indices, ESG scores and environmental capital spending; use staggered state business-combination laws as exogenous variation in takeover protection.
ideas.disconfirming: Takeover protection goes with lower sustainability investment or lower returns on it.

ideas.hypothesis: Rises in foreign institutional ownership increase the share of women and outsiders on boards, especially in countries with homogeneous traditional boards such as Japan.

sources.role: mechanism: foreign institutional investors pushing governance reform in Japan
measure: board attributes

ideas.test: Japanese and Korean listed firms 2005-2019; use MSCI index inclusion as an instrument for foreign ownership; outcomes are the shares of women and outside directors.
ideas.disconfirming: Foreign ownership has no effect on board diversity.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms whose governance is less open (few outside directors, weak disclosure, little stakeholder exchange) fail more often, consistent with the view that governance systems need information exchange with their environment to avoid decay.

sources.role: mechanism: governance as an open dissipative structure needing exchange through internal and external governance
mechanism: corporation as a viable system dependent on relations with super-systems

ideas.test: Build an openness index for listed firms (outside directors, disclosure score, institutional ownership, stakeholder reporting) and estimate hazard models for bankruptcy or delisting 2000-2018, controlling for standard distress predictors.
ideas.disconfirming: The openness index adds nothing to standard distress predictors.

ideas.hypothesis: Audit committee members with prior social ties to the CEO are less likely to catch or report misstatements, reflecting loyalty-driven deference rather than lack of expertise.

sources.role: mechanism: obedience and loyalty to the CEO from behavioral economics
mechanism: bias of monitors under conflicting pressures

ideas.test: US firms 2003-2018 with BoardEx social ties and Audit Analytics restatements; logit of restatements on the share of CEO-tied audit committee members, controlling for financial expertise.
ideas.disconfirming: Ties are unrelated to restatements.

ideas.hypothesis: Stakeholder engagement buffers the negative effect of environmental uncertainty on organizational performance, with the buffer working through governance quality.

sources.role: mechanism: governance mediating between external environment and performance
setting: stakeholder roles in governance
mechanism: coordinating stakeholder interests

ideas.test: Survey of about 300 firms measuring perceived uncertainty, engagement practices and performance, analyzed with moderated mediation SEM; alternatively, archival GRI stakeholder-engagement disclosures with industry volatility.
ideas.disconfirming: Engagement does not moderate the uncertainty-performance link.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries with proportional electoral systems adopt weaker mandatory disclosure requirements, because coalition politics favors insiders and organized labor over outside investors.

sources.role: mechanism: governance rooted in particular politics; the state as key actor
mechanism: political economy of governance arrangements

ideas.test: Cross-section of about 50 countries with electoral system data (Database of Political Institutions) and securities-law disclosure indices; regressions with legal-origin controls.
ideas.disconfirming: No relation after legal-origin controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Employee trust in the top management team mediates the link between governance quality and strategy execution, so firms with high employee trust turn governance improvements into larger performance gains.

sources.role: mechanism: second agency relationship between management and employees
mechanism: internal organization determines governance quality

ideas.test: Link employee ratings of senior leadership (e.g., Glassdoor) to firm governance scores and ROA for listed firms 2010-2019; mediation analysis.
ideas.disconfirming: Employee trust does not mediate the governance-performance link.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms that write stakeholder co-governance values into their charters or codes face fewer fraud enforcement actions.

sources.role: mechanism: corporate values and shareholder-stakeholder co-governance
mechanism: trust within the firm

ideas.test: Text-analyze charters and codes of conduct of Chinese or US listed firms for stakeholder values; match to CSRC or SEC enforcement records; logit with firm controls.
ideas.disconfirming: Value statements are unrelated or positively related to fraud (window dressing).

ideas.hypothesis: Better governance disclosure raises minority shareholder participation and dissent at general meetings.

sources.role: setting: transparency at Bucharest Stock Exchange listed firms
measure: governance disclosure index
mechanism: disclosure and minority shareholders

ideas.test: Emerging-market listed firms with AGM attendance and vote records; regress turnout and dissent on disclosure scores, using exchange disclosure rule changes for identification.
ideas.disconfirming: Disclosure is unrelated to participation or dissent.

ideas.hypothesis: In transition-economy firms marked by insider control, foreign institutional ownership above a threshold weakens insider-dominated boards and raises performance.

sources.role: mechanism: foreign institutions pressing for reform
setting: improving internal governance in Chinese listed firms
setting: governance quality in SEE countries

ideas.test: CEE/SEE listed firms 2005-2018 from Orbis; threshold regressions of board insider share and ROA on foreign institutional ownership.
ideas.disconfirming: No threshold effect.

ideas.hypothesis: Stronger CEO equity incentives reduce value-destroying diversification and increase refocusing divestitures.

sources.role: finding: diversification tied to weak governance; refocusing with better monitoring
mechanism: compensation giving CEOs little incentive to improve results

ideas.test: ExecuComp CEO delta and vega with Compustat segment data 1992-2018; panel regressions of segment-count changes and divestitures on incentives.
ideas.disconfirming: Equity incentives are unrelated to diversification.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries with more multinational subsidiary presence adopt national governance codes earlier and with more Anglo-American provisions.

sources.role: finding: question of global convergence in governance disclosure
mechanism: performative diffusion of governance models
setting: calls for universal governance standards

ideas.test: Code adoption dates and content from the ECGI database for about 80 countries; hazard model with inward FDI stock by origin country.
ideas.disconfirming: MNC presence predicts neither adoption timing nor code content.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms whose boards met more often during the 2008 financial crisis recovered market value faster and had fewer covenant violations.

sources.role: setting: governance failures exposed by the global financial crisis
mechanism: board effectiveness

ideas.test: US and European listed firms with board meeting counts from proxy statements 2006-2011; difference-in-differences on recovery of market value and covenant violations.
ideas.disconfirming: More meetings are unrelated or negatively related to recovery.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms incorporated in states with constituency statutes engage stakeholders more than Delaware-incorporated firms, holding headquarters state constant.

sources.role: setting: corporate law and shareholder primacy versus stakeholder theory
setting: stakeholder roles

ideas.test: US listed firms with incorporation state and stakeholder engagement scores from ESG data; compare across incorporation regimes and around reincorporation events.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference by incorporation regime.

ideas.hypothesis: CEOs from Confucian-heritage regions behave more like stewards, with lower excess pay and perk consumption at given monitoring intensity.

sources.role: mechanism: moral concepts of loyalty and responsibility in boards
setting: Chinese governance research
mechanism: corporate values in governance

ideas.test: Chinese listed firms with CEO birthplace; measure Confucian intensity of birthplace; regress perk consumption and excess pay on it with firm controls.
ideas.disconfirming: No relation.
